findings.quote: and no one defended this act as just.
findings.problem: The sentence runs across the chapter seam: διεδικαίου δὲ τὴν πρᾶξιν ταύτην οὐδεὶς | Ἀλεξάνδρου (first word of ch. 3) = 'no one justified this act of Alexander's'. The genitive belongs here, not at the start of ch. 3.
findings.proposed_fix: and no one defended this act of Alexander’s as just.

units.note: Seam word Ἀλεξάνδρου is printed at the head of ch. 3 but completes this sentence; see ch. 3 finding.

findings.quote: After Alexander’s campaign, they therefore, after a short time and with some help received, once again lived in their homeland in safety.
findings.problem: 'After Alexander's campaign' is invented from the seam word Ἀλεξάνδρου, which ends the previous chapter's sentence (τὴν πρᾶξιν ταύτην οὐδεὶς Ἀλεξάνδρου). This sentence is just τοιγαροῦν βραχεῖ χρόνῳ τυχόντες ἐπικουρίας τινὸς αὖθις ᾤκουν τὴν πατρίδα μετ᾽ ἀσφαλείας.
findings.proposed_fix: Therefore, after a short time, receiving some help, they once again lived in their homeland in safety.

findings.quote: For all who fall into unexpected disasters should be counted as unfortunate, both collectively and individually;
findings.problem: The μὲν … δέ contrast is between ἀκληρεῖν ('to be unlucky', all who meet unexpected calamities) and ἀτυχεῖν ('to be unfortunate', only those disgraced by their own folly). Translating both as 'unfortunate' turns the distinction into a contradiction.
findings.proposed_fix: For all who fall into unexpected disasters, both collectively and individually, should be counted as unlucky;

findings.problem: Lacuna smoothed: Greek reads Φωκεῖς, ... εῖς, Λοκροί — an ethnic ending in -εῖς is lost between Phocians and Locrians (often restored as Euboeans).

findings.quote: Not only in number, but in every way, they were not merely unfortunate in the ordinary sense, but suffered a shameful sort of misfortune, as dishonorable as possible.
findings.problem: Lacunae smoothed: ... μὴ μόνον κατὰ τὸ πλῆθος ... τῶν πρότερον, ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ ... ἐπίπαν — gaps before and inside the phrase, and 'in every way' is invented. Also negation softened: οὐκ ἠκλήρησαν, ἀλλ᾽ ἠτύχησαν = 'they were NOT (merely) unlucky but suffered misfortune'; 'not merely unfortunate' blurs the ἀκληρεῖν/ἀτυχεῖν distinction just defined.
findings.proposed_fix: [...] not only in the number [...] of earlier ones, but also in [...]; in a word, they were not unlucky but suffered a misfortune as shameful and disgraceful as could be.

findings.quote: Thus, stripped of all good things, some perished from hunger, while others, driven to desperation, even then took rods and axes into the cities [...]
findings.problem: Lacunae smoothed and text invented: Greek is ... ἅμα. τοιγαροῦν στερηθέντες πάντων τῶν καλῶν οἱ μὲν ὑπὸ στέ[...], ἔνιοι δὲ καὶ δ[...]ντες εἰς τὰς πόλεις τότε παρεδέξαντο ῥάβδους καὶ πελέκεις ἐθελο[...]. 'perished from hunger' and 'driven to desperation' have no basis in the fragments. παρεδέξαντο = 'admitted/received' (the Roman fasces into their cities), not 'took'; ἐθελο- suggests 'willingly' but is broken.
findings.proposed_fix: [...] Thus, deprived of all good things, some [...], while others [...] then admitted the rods and axes into their cities [...]

findings.quote: because of the excess of their own mistakes, if it is right to say so.
findings.problem: εἰ χρὴ λέγειν ἰδίων qualifies the word 'own' specifically ('if one should call them their own'), which the next γάρ-sentence explains (the many were misled; the leaders were guilty). 'if it is right to say so' loses the point.
findings.proposed_fix: because of the excess of their own mistakes—if one should call them their own.

units.note: Fragmentary chapter (Constantinian excerpts); several gaps. 'ἀπιστίαν' could be 'faithlessness' rather than 'distrust' but not flagged (lexical).

findings.quote: when it was above all right to conceal the mistakes of the Greeks.
findings.problem: οἷς καθῆκον ἦν μάλιστα πάντων περιστέλλειν refers to the writer (ἡμῖν): critics will say that I, of all people, ought to cover up the Greeks' faults. The impersonal English loses whose duty it was.
findings.proposed_fix: when I, of all people, ought to have concealed the mistakes of the Greeks.

findings.quote: For the more widely the transmission of what is written reaches people, and the longer it lasts,
findings.problem: The ὅσῳ … τοσούτῳ clause compares written record with speech: ἡ διὰ τῶν ὑπομνημάτων παράδοσις τῶν πρὸς καιρὸν λεγομένων = 'written transmission, compared with what is said for the occasion'. The comparand is dropped.
findings.proposed_fix: For the more widely, and the longer, written record reaches than words spoken for the moment,

findings.quote: But those who love learning seek continuity and look forward to hearing the end of the account;
findings.problem: ζητεῖν δὲ τοὺς φιλομαθοῦντας … ἱμείρειν … συνεκτρέχειν are infinitives still governed by φάσκοντες: this is the critics' claim, which Polybius then rejects (ἐμοὶ δ᾽ οὐχ οὕτως δοκεῖ). 'But' presents it as the author's own view.
findings.proposed_fix: And, they say, those who love learning seek continuity and long to hear the end of the subject;

findings.quote: rests for those who labor hard [...]
findings.problem: Not a lacuna: the phrase is completed by ἀνδρῶν, printed as the first word of ch. 6 (τοῖς φιλοπόνοις τῶν | ἀνδρῶν = 'for industrious men'). The gap marker is false.
findings.proposed_fix: rests for men who love hard work.

units.note: Seam with ch. 6: ἀνδρῶν belongs to the last sentence here.

findings.quote: For those who are diligent in such matters, the greatest historians of old seem to me
findings.problem: 'For those who are diligent in such matters' is invented from the seam word ἀνδρῶν, which ends ch. 5's sentence. The sentence begins διὸ καὶ τῶν ἀρχαίων συγγραφέων οἱ λογιώτατοι = 'That is why the most learned of the ancient historians'; the inferential διό is lost.
findings.proposed_fix: That is why the most learned of the ancient historians seem to me

units.note: καταλλήλους πράξεις ('fitting events') more nearly means 'corresponding/contemporaneous events'; outside the error classes, not flagged.
